# Worker Stage — Ground-Truth Digest

**1) How the worker stage renders today**
Two surfaces read the same `session.workers`: the right rail `<AgentSidebar/>` (rendered prop-less, gated by `hasWorkers`, at `workspace/page.tsx:125`) and the in-body review block inside `ProgressiveFlow.tsx`. Phase is driven by `deployPhase = session?.worker_deploy_phase` (`ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1151`). Pre-deploy (`'ready'`): a `PhaseDivider` (1971) + `<TeamDeployBanner>` (1976–1989, file `TeamDeployBanner.tsx`) showing the assembled crew with swap/add/remove + the 출항 CTA → `onDeployWorkers` (1259). Post-deploy (`'deployed'`): the one-at-a-time review stepper (2086–2157).

**2) AgentSidebar — content + status→label**
`AgentSidebar.tsx`. Header "분석 팀 / Analysis Team" + live count, a 2px gold progress bar (`--gradient-gold`, width = doneCount/total, 474–482), then `AgentRow`s. Status logic: `isWorkingStatus` = `running|sent|waiting_response` (28); `isPending` = `pending|ai_preparing` (21). **Pending workers are filtered OUT** (`visibleWorkers`, 433) — they only slide in once active. `StatusBadge` (31–60): working→spinning `live` pill; `done`→emerald check; `waiting_input`→gold "입력 필요"; `error`→"오류"; else→"standby". Rows carry a live ticker (`tickersFor`/`stream_text` tail, 109–121), auto-reveal-on-done (124–136), and multi-stage grouping via `groupedByStage` (437).

**3) Review stepper + WorkerReportBlock**
Stepper at `ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2086–2157`: workers sorted by `step_index`; `reviewCursor` selects `current`; clickable dots (active = `w-5 h-2 bg-[var(--accent)]`, handled = `bg-accent/45`, else `bg-border`, 2110–2118); "N명 남음" counts `!handled && done` (2096); `handled` = `approved != null || status==='error'` (2095); slide via `AnimatePresence mode="wait"` x:±14 (2124–2127); Prev/Later nav (2142). `WorkerReportBlock` (`WorkerCard.tsx:149`) is finding-first: per-status early returns (running/sent/pending/error/waiting_input), then the **done body** (462+): color line in persona color, avatar, name+role+Lv, task, validation badge, completion_note, "핵심 발견/Key finding" box (`extractKeyFinding`, 521), "전체 초안 보기" modal, and Exclude / **Apply→Next** buttons (gold gradient, 592–603) that call `onApprove/onReject` then `onAdvance` — plus reassign via pool modal.

**4) WorkerTask.status values + approved flag** (`types.ts:737`)
`WorkerStatus = pending | ai_preparing | running | done | error | waiting_input | sent | waiting_response | validation_failed`. Meaning: `pending`=assigned, not started; `ai_preparing`=AI auxiliary pre-pass for self/human tasks (set in `deployWorkers`, store:1010); `running`=executing/streaming; `waiting_input`=needs user (self/human decision); `sent`/`waiting_response`=external human dispatched; `done`=result ready; `validation_failed`=quality<70; `error`. `approved: boolean|null` (785): null=unreviewed, true=반영(included), false=제외(excluded). **No pre-scout field exists yet** — closest is `ai_preliminary?: string|null` (795) + `assignment_reason` (812). Lifecycle: `initWorkers`→`status:'pending'`,`phase:'ready'` (store:916,986); `deployWorkers`→`'ai_preparing'` or `'running'`,`phase:'deployed'` (store:1000–1010).

**5) Tokens / motion** (`globals.css`)
`--accent:#96782e` (dark `#d4b968`), `--accent-light`, `--bp-ink:#1a2a3a` (navy), `--bp-ink-soft #4a6180`, `--bg:#f8f7f5`, `--surface:#fff`, `--border-subtle:#eeebe6`, `--gradient-gold`, `--gradient-gold-subtle`, `--gradient-gold-text`, `--gradient-surface`, `--shadow-xs…xl`, `--font-display: 'Noto Serif KR', Georgia, serif`, `--ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)`, `--ease-wave: cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)`. Motion: `EASE = [0.32,0.72,0,1]` and `SPRING = {stiffness:400,damping:30}` (`constants.ts:3-4`).

**6) Why sidebar↔body connection is invisible**
There is data linkage but **zero shared focus state**: the stepper's `reviewCursor` is local to `ProgressiveFlow` and never written anywhere the sidebar can read; clicking a sidebar `AgentRow` only toggles its OWN local `expandedId` (530) — it does NOT move `reviewCursor`, and the body never highlights the sidebar row for `current`. The only cross-surface link that exists is `useAgentAttentionStore` (`hovered: {kind:'agent'|'section'|'sentence'}`), but it is **hover/done-only** (`onHoverStart` gated by `isDone`, 150) and is used for draft↔agent attribution, not for review focus. So "which agent's card am I looking at" and "that agent in the rail" are two disconnected highlights. Also pending/pre-scout agents are hidden (433), so "assigned vs working" never reads.

**7) Components/utilities to reuse**
`useAgentAttentionStore` (extend with a `focusedWorkerId` channel — the natural home for sidebar↔stepper sync), `AgentVisuals` (`TypingDots`, `AvatarRipple`, `ShimmerBar`, `AttentionFlash`, `tickersFor`, `useAttentionPulse`), `WorkerAvatar`, `extractKeyFinding`, `renderMd`, `localizePersona`/`personaName`, `StatusBadge`/`StageDivider`/`StageTransitionBanner` (AgentSidebar), `WorkerReportBlock`/`ResultModal` (WorkerCard), `TeamDeployBanner`, `PhaseDivider`, `useWorkerActions` (approve/reject/retry/submit), `useWorkers`/`useWorkerContext` (WorkerPanel), and the `agent-lv` CSS class + `--gradient-gold`/`--shadow-*` tokens for premium polish.

concepts.name: CREW MANIFEST — Ship's Log
concepts.one_line: The sidebar becomes an editorial ship's log where each agent is a roster entry advancing through voyage stages; selecting one draws a single gold ligature thread that carries the roster row into the body review card, so status and action read as one continuous object.
concepts.big_idea: Today there are two disconnected highlights and pending crew is hidden, so "assigned vs working" never reads (AgentSidebar.tsx:433 filters out pending; reviewCursor at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:965 is local and never reaches the rail). The organizing idea is a CREW MANIFEST: the sidebar is a calm serif roster — a ship's log — where every assigned agent has a permanent berth from the moment of casting (pending) onward, and each berth carries a small voyage-stage marker. There is exactly ONE focused crew member at a time, and a single gold hairline "ligature" visually links the focused roster berth to its open report in the body. It feels premium because it is restrained editorial typography (Noto Serif KR display for names, --bp-ink, generous 14px row rhythm) plus ONE expensive gesture — the thread — rather than a dashboard of badges. The connection is made obvious by making the rail and the card literally share a continuation line and a synchronized highlight, mediated by extending the store channel that already exists (useAgentAttentionStore) with a focusedWorkerId — no new plumbing.
concepts.sidebar_design: Rebuild AgentSidebar as a vertical "manifest" with a left voyage-rail. Header stays "분석 팀 / Analysis Team" (AgentSidebar.tsx:450) + the 2px gold progress bar (474-482) but gains a second micro-line: a journey legend "배정 → 정찰 → 출항 → 작업 → 검토" rendered as 5 dim dots that fill gold as the crew advances. Then a single continuous vertical hairline (1px, --bp-ink-faint) runs down the left edge through ALL rows — the "log spine." Each AgentRow becomes a berth: [stage-node on the spine] [WorkerAvatar sm] [serif name + Lv.] [one status line]. CRITICAL CHANGE: stop filtering pending — remove the visibleWorkers filter (433) so the full crew shows from casting; pending/pre-scout berths render at 0.55 opacity with a hollow spine-node, working berths at full opacity with a filled pulsing node, done berths get an emerald-filled node and the existing completion sweep (175-183). Berth layout per row: name in --font-display 13px, role/status in 11px --bp-ink-soft. When a worker is focusedWorkerId, its berth gets the gold ligature treatment (see connection mechanic). Keep StageDivider/groupedByStage (437) for multi-stage; the log spine simply segments at each StageDivider.
concepts.connection_mechanic: Extend useAgentAttentionStore (useAgentAttentionStore.ts:35) with a NEW orthogonal channel: `focusedWorkerId: string|null` + `setFocusedWorker(id|null)` — separate from `hovered` (which stays for draft↔agent attribution) and from `sticky`. Wire it both ways: (1) the body stepper writes it — at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2091 after computing `current`, a useEffect calls setFocusedWorker(current.id) whenever cursor changes; the dots (2111) and Prev/Later (2143) already move the cursor, so they now also move rail focus. (2) the rail reads + writes it — clicking an AgentRow whose worker is `done`/`waiting_input`/`error` (i.e. reviewable) sets focusedWorker AND moves the stepper: pass an `onFocus(workerId)` prop from ProgressiveFlow that runs `setReviewCursor(ordered.findIndex(w=>w.id===id))`. THE LIGATURE: the focused berth renders, on its right edge, an SVG gold hairline that exits the row and a matching stub enters the body card's left color-line (WorkerCard.tsx:273 already draws a persona-color `w-px self-stretch` — recolor it to --gradient-gold when focused and add a `layoutId="crew-ligature"` motion element shared between the rail berth's right node and the card's left line). framer-motion `layoutId` makes the gold node visually FLY from rail to card on focus change — one continuous object. Both surfaces also share the persona color: berth node, ligature, and card spine all use `worker.persona.color`, with the focused one promoted to --gradient-gold. Result: "that row in the rail" and "this card in the body" are unmistakably the same crew member, connected by a literal drawn line.
concepts.deploy_ceremony: Keep TeamDeployBanner (TeamDeployBanner.tsx) and its CTA (relabel back to "출항 / Set sail" at line 437) but stage the moment. On click of onDeployWorkers (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1259), before deployWorkers() runs, play a 1.1s "casting off" overlay scoped to the worker column: (1) the rail's log spine draws itself top-to-bottom with the existing `draw-line 1s var(--ease-spring)` keyframe (globals.css:351) — the voyage line is "charted"; (2) each berth's stage-node advances from 정찰(pre-scout) to 출항 in a staggered ripple (stagger 0.07s, the banner's existing cadence at TeamDeployBanner.tsx:70) using AvatarRipple (AgentVisuals); (3) a single --gradient-gold sweep crosses the whole rail once (reuse the StageTransitionBanner sweep, AgentSidebar.tsx:308-314). The banner itself does NOT just vanish — it `layout` collapses upward (height→0, --ease-wave) as the first berths flip to `running`, so the crew "boards" the rail. The deploy ping already fires (1267); add store.recordCheckpoint('crew_set') is already there (1265). Net: the gate stays a real gate, but pressing it is a scene — the line is charted, the crew boards, the rail comes alive.
concepts.prescout_surfacing: The pre-scout writes to the EXISTING `ai_preliminary` field (types.ts:795) — no new schema. During Q&A after initWorkers (status 'pending', phase 'ready'), a light pass populates `ai_preliminary` with a 1-sentence angle per agent (token-frugal, NOT the task). In the rail, a pending berth with `ai_preliminary` shows its stage-node at the "정찰 / scouting" position (node #2 of 5, half-filled gold ring) and renders the angle as a quiet 11px italic --bp-ink-soft line under the name, prefixed with a small Compass icon (already imported in TeamDeployBanner.tsx:5) — e.g. "정찰: 가격 민감도부터 보겠습니다." This reuses the assignment_reason rendering pattern (TeamDeployBanner.tsx:154-158). A pending berth WITHOUT a pre-scout yet shows a 2-dot TypingDots (AgentVisuals) "정찰 중" shimmer. So by deploy time every berth already shows a direction; "light" stays legible because it's one italic line, visually subordinate to the post-deploy live ticker.
concepts.status_system: Map WorkerTask.status + approved to a 5-node voyage marker on the log spine, each with a precise visual: (1) ASSIGNED — status 'pending', no ai_preliminary → hollow ring, --bp-ink-faint, berth 0.55 opacity, label "배정됨/Assigned". (2) PRE-SCOUTING — 'pending'/'ai_preparing' WITH ai_preliminary → half-gold ring + Compass + italic angle, label "정찰/Scouting". (3) READY/STANDBY — 'pending' post-scout pre-deploy → solid faint-gold ring, label "대기/Standby" (replaces the old "standby" badge at AgentSidebar.tsx:59). (4) WORKING — 'running'/'sent'/'waiting_response' (isWorkingStatus, 27) → filled pulsing persona-color node + AvatarRipple + ShimmerBar + live ticker (keep 109-121), label spinner "live" (35-39). (5a) AWAITING-REVIEW — 'done' but approved==null → emerald-filled node with a small gold pulse-ring meaning "needs your call," label "검토 대기/Review" (this is the state today's "N명 남음" counts, ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2096). (5b) REVIEWED — 'done' + approved===true → solid emerald check (43-46); approved===false → emerald node dimmed to 0.5 + a thin strike, label "제외/Excluded". Plus 'waiting_input' → gold "입력 필요" node (keep 48-54); 'error' → red node + inline retry (keep 238-247); 'validation_failed' → amber node. The node IS the status language — shared identically on the body card spine.

concepts.big_idea: One organizing idea: every agent is a STATION on a ship's bridge, and the bridge (sidebar) and the captain's table (body review card) are physically wired together. A single shared focus channel + a drawn tie-line. Concretely:
1. EXTEND useAgentAttentionStore (useAgentAttentionStore.ts:35) with `focusedWorkerId: string | null` and `setFocusedWorker(id, origin: 'rail'|'body')`. This is the natural home the digest already identified — it is the only cross-surface store, but today it's hover/done-only.

In ProgressiveFlow.tsx, make reviewCursor DERIVE from focusedWorkerId instead of being free: when a station is clicked, setFocusedWorker(w.id,'rail'); an effect maps focusedWorkerId → the index in the ordered list and calls setReviewCursor (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2090-2097). Conversely, when the body dots/Prev/Next move the cursor (2111,2143,2149), write focusedWorkerId = ordered[cursor].id with origin 'body'. One source of truth, two writers, no loops (guard on origin).

The VISIBLE wire: when a station is focused, (a) the station row gets a left gold spine — a 3px-wide bar on its left edge in --gradient-gold that animates scaleY 0→1; (b) the docked body card grows the SAME gold spine on its left (WorkerReportBlock already has a per-persona color line at WorkerCard.tsx:481 — widen it to 3px and tint --accent when focused); (c) a hairline "tie-line" SVG path draws from the station's right edge toward the body card. concepts.one_line: The right rail stops being a list of cards and becomes a vertical star-chart: each agent is a charted waypoint on the voyage line, the pre-scout shows as a faint pencilled bearing under each star, "set sail" lights the whole route at once, and clicking any star draws a single lit gold leg straight to the focused review card in the body — sidebar and body are now visibly one constellation.
concepts.big_idea: Argus already owns a nautical chart language (VoyageChart.tsx:48 — the 해도, with logged points as filled gold dots, checkpoints as hollow rings, the "current" node ringed, anchored legs flagged). The worker rail today throws that away and reverts to a generic stack of bordered cards (AgentSidebar AgentRow, 138-249) — exactly the "generic AI dashboard" we're told NOT to be. The big idea: re-skin the rail as a STAR-CHART of the crew. The voyage line runs top-to-bottom; each agent is a star/waypoint pinned on it in step_index order; the line between stars IS the progress bar (it currently floats disconnected at 474). The chart is the navigator — it carries rich per-agent status as the star's own state (unlit→pencilled→lit→flagged), and it IS the thing that connects to the body: selecting a star runs a lit gold leg out of the rail toward the focused review card. It feels premium because nothing is a "widget" — it's one continuous drawn route on aged-chart vellum, ink + gold, that earns the voyage DNA instead of decorating around it. Reuse, not reinvention: same dot/ring/flag vocabulary, same --accent gold, same EASE.

concepts.status_system: One node-glyph vocabulary mapped 1:1 to real WorkerStatus (types.ts:737), borrowing VoyageChart's dot/ring/flag legend (VoyageChart.tsx:136-158) so it's already a learned language: • pending (assigned, no scout yet) → small HOLLOW grey ring, dim 0.55, line2 = assigned task. • ai_preliminary_status 'scouting' (pre-scout running) → hollow ring + slow pencil shimmer, line2 = "sketching an angle". • pre-scout ready (still pending) → HALF node (ink+gold pencil tick) + italic bearing line. • ai_preparing → same half/scouting treatment (AI aux pre-pass, store:1010) — honest, it IS preparing. • running / sent / waiting_response → LIT node pulsing in persona color + AvatarRipple + live stream tail (reuse isWorkingStatus, AgentSidebar:27; the gold spine has climbed to this star). • waiting_input → lit node with a gold pulsing dot + "입력 필요 / Input" pill (keep StatusBadge logic, AgentSidebar:48-54) — the one star that asks the captain for a heading. • done → SOLID GOLD FILLED star (the VoyageChart "logged point", 138) + completion_note italic; if awaiting review (approved==null) a faint gold ring orbits it = "logged, not yet confirmed". • approved===true → solid star with a small Flag/anchor (reuse Flag, VoyageChart:116) = "course reflected in the draft". • approved===false → hollow dimmed node, struck (the "abandoned course" treatment, VoyageChart:153) = excluded. • error / validation_failed → node ringed red + inline Retry (keep AgentSidebar:238-247). The captain reads the whole journey assigned→scouting→ready→[set sail]→working→done→awaiting-review→reviewed as the star's own life on the line — no separate legend needed because it mirrors the chart they already know.

concepts.name: 단일 항로 (THE SINGLE SPINE / "항로")
concepts.one_line: The sidebar becomes a literal vertical voyage-route — each agent is a station on one gold spine; pre-scout glows faintly under its node, "출항" lights the whole route, work flows down it, and clicking any station docks its review card to that exact node in the body so the rail and the card are one continuous line.
concepts.big_idea: Stop treating the rail and the review stepper as two surfaces to "connect" — make them two ends of ONE drawn line. The right rail (workspace/page.tsx:120 `w-72 xl:w-80` sticky rail) becomes a vertical "항로" (route): a single 2px spine in `--gradient-gold` runs top-to-bottom with a node per agent (one node = one WorkerTask, ordered by `step_index`). The body review stepper is not a separate widget — it is the *currently-docked station* of that same route, rendered inline in the column but visually tethered to its rail node by a shared gold thread + a synced `focusedWorkerId`. Premium because: (1) it is a single editorial object, not a dashboard of cards — serif station labels, generous vertical rhythm, one continuous gold line that literally draws itself as the voyage progresses (reusing the existing `draw-line`/`bar-grow` motion language at globals.css:351/410); (2) the connection is *structural*, not a highlight bolted on — you are always looking at one route, and "which station am I at" is answered by where the line is lit, not by two independent glows; (3) it turns the agreed metaphor (reframe→...→이타카) into the actual geometry of the screen. concepts.sidebar_design: AgentSidebar.tsx is reworked from a list of bordered cards into a vertical route. To the right of each node: station label block — serif `--font-display` agent name at 13px, role/Lv as a quiet sub-line (reuse `agent-lv` class + `localizePersona`). Below the label, a single status line (the rich status, see status_system) and, when working, the existing live ticker (`tickersFor`/`stream_text` tail, reuse 109-121 verbatim) and `ShimmerBar`. CRITICAL CHANGE: remove the `visibleWorkers` filter at AgentSidebar.tsx:433 — pending/pre-scout agents are NO LONGER hidden. The whole point of a route is you see all stations from the start as faint, unlit nodes; they brighten as the voyage reaches them. Header keeps "분석 팀 / Analysis Team" eyebrow but the 2px horizontal progress bar (474-482) is removed (the spine IS the progress now). Stage grouping (`groupedByStage`, 437) survives as labeled spine *segments* — the StageDivider (343) becomes a station marker on the spine ("Stage Ⅱ — 검증") with the gold line passing through it.
concepts.connection_mechanic: Extend `useAgentAttentionStore` (useAgentAttentionStore.ts:53) with ONE new channel — `focusedWorkerId: string | null` + `setFocusedWorker(id)` — the natural shared-focus home the digest already identified. concepts.deploy_ceremony: Kept as a hard gate, designed as a real scene — "출항" (set sail). concepts.status_system: Per-station visual language mapped to real WorkerStatus (types.ts:737) + `approved`, expressed as node-ring state + one status line. (1) pending (assigned, pre-deploy): hollow desaturated ring, persona color @35%, label dim; status line = task name (reuse 233-235). (2) pre-scout present (pending + `ai_preliminary` set): hollow **dashed gold** ring; sub-line shows the angle (see prescout). (3) ai_preparing: ring pulses, `TypingDots`, line "AI 참고자료 준비 중" (reuse WorkerCard.tsx:211 wording). (4) running / sent / waiting_response (`isWorkingStatus`, 27-29): **lit node** — solid persona-color ring with `AvatarRipple` + `ShimmerBar` on the spine segment below it, live ticker line, and the spine gold-fill animates DOWN to this node (the "work flowing down the route"); badge = the existing spinning `live` pill (35-39). (5) waiting_input: gold pulsing dot + "입력 필요" (reuse 48-54) — node ring turns solid gold (`--accent`), and because it needs the captain, it auto-becomes the focused station. (6) done (un-reviewed): emerald check node (reuse 41-46), spine segment above it now solid gold; sub-line = `completion_note` (222-226); a faint "검토 대기 / awaiting review" tag. (7) reviewed-approved (`approved===true`): node fills solid gold with a small "반영" tag (mirror WorkerCard.tsx:494); spine segment locks gold. (8) reviewed-excluded (`approved===false`): node dims to `--border-subtle`, label `line-through`-soft, "제외" tag (mirror 495) — the station is visibly skipped on the route. (9) error: red ring + inline Retry (reuse 238-247) — a "rough water" station. (10) validation_failed: amber ring, "품질 확인 필요" (reuse WorkerCard.tsx:193). concepts.one_line: The sidebar becomes the ship's crew register and the body's review dots ARE that register's entries — one shared `focusedWorkerId` channel binds the row you click to the card you read, with a brief gold thread drawn between them; the deploy gate becomes a real "출항" muster; pre-scout shows as a one-line angle under each name.
concepts.big_idea: Keep both surfaces (AgentSidebar rail + the in-body one-at-a-time stepper at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2086) but treat them as ONE instrument with two faces: the sidebar is the *register* (who, status, the angle they took); the body is the *open page* (the full finding for whichever crew member the captain is reading). The reason this feels premium and not like a generic dashboard: instead of inventing a new connection widget, we promote the data they already share (session.workers) into a single shared FOCUS state, then make that focus *visible* with one disciplined gold thread and a mirrored focus-ring. Nothing flashes everywhere; exactly one row and exactly one card are lit at a time, in the accent gold, on the slow EASE spring. The register reads like an editorial masthead (serif name, quiet role, one italic scouting line), not a status grid — that restraint is the expense.
concepts.sidebar_design: AgentSidebar.tsx becomes a register, not a filtered live-feed. Header keeps "분석 팀 / Analysis Team" + the gold doneCount progress bar (:474-482) unchanged. Rows become selectable (not just done-rows): the whole row is a button that sets focus.
concepts.connection_mechanic: Add a single shared channel to useAgentAttentionStore: `focusedWorkerId: string | null` + `setFocus(id)` / `clearFocus()`. This store already lives session-long and is already imported by both AgentSidebar (:15) and the body — it is the natural and lowest-risk home (digest §7). Bind it bidirectionally to the stepper's existing `reviewCursor`: in ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2086-2157, derive `cursor` from `focusedWorkerId` (find its index in `ordered`) instead of local-only state, and on dot/Prev/Later click call `setFocus(ordered[i].id)` (keep reviewCursor as the fallback when focus is null). When focus changes, a thin gold path (`stroke:url(#gradient-gold-stroke)`, 1.5px) is drawn from the focused sidebar row's status-rail (right edge) to the focused card's color-line (left edge, WorkerCard.tsx:481). Implemented as a fixed-position SVG overlay that reads both elements' `getBoundingClientRect()` (rows carry `data-roster-id={worker.id}`, the card carries `data-focus-card`); the path animates `pathLength: 0→1` over 0.5s on EASE, holds ~700ms, then fades. One thread, gold, slow — a drawn line on a chart, faithful to the blueprint/voyage DNA. Hover keeps the existing `hovered` attribution channel untouched (it is done-only, draft↔agent); focus is the new, explicit, click-driven channel — they never fight.

Motion uses `--ease-wave` (the cinematic cubic the globals reserve for reveals, :319/334). concept.big_idea: Today there are two disconnected highlights and pending crew is hidden, so "assigned vs working" never reads (AgentSidebar.tsx:433 filters out pending; reviewCursor at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:965 is local and never reaches the rail). votes.verdict: On pure craft this is the most expensive-feeling option I can imagine on this stack, and it earns it by RESTRAINT rather than addition. The core craft thesis — "one log spine + ONE expensive gesture (the gold ligature) instead of a dashboard of badges" — is exactly the dawn-harbor DNA's value system. It reads as editorial, not as an AI dashboard. Verified against source: it builds on real primitives rather than inventing chrome. The serif berth name uses --font-display (globals.css:57, Noto Serif KR), the 2px gold progress bar already exists (AgentSidebar.tsx:474-482), the completion sweep it reuses is real (AgentSidebar.tsx:175-183), the persona-color left spine it recolors-to-gold is real (WorkerCard.tsx:273 `w-px self-stretch`), draw-line keyframe is real (globals.css:344-351), and the focus-ring style it reuses is real (AgentSidebar.tsx:164). Hierarchy is genuinely premium: name in 13px serif --bp-ink, status in 11px --bp-ink-soft, pending crew subordinated to 0.55 opacity so the rail reads as a calm backdrop with one lit member — that is the "generous whitespace + one focal point" move, not a wall of equal-weight rows. The VoyageNode (5-state spine marker) as the single status language, shared identically on rail and card, is the kind of disciplined system-design that makes a thing feel intentional. The ligature layoutId — one gold node physically flying rail→card — is precisely "one expensive gesture" and it directly answers Q3's "status↔action as one continuous object" in the most literal, beautiful way available in framer-motion. Motion specs are correct and consistent: EASE [0.32,0.72,0,1] matches the stepper's real slide (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2127), --ease-spring node pops, SPRING layout reflow. The deploy ceremony (spine self-draws, berths ripple 정찰→출항, one gold sweep, banner layout-collapses upward) is a real SCENE, not a speed bump — high craft. Where it loses a half-notch on craft (rounded down, not enough to drop to 4): the ASCII mockup's rail is denser than the prose claims — five berths each with a 11px italic pre-scout line, a voyage node, an avatar, name+Lv, AND a status line, plus a 5-dot journey legend AND the progress bar AND the header pill, is a LOT of vertical furniture for a fixed-right rail; the "calm serif roster" risks becoming busy precisely because every berth now carries a node + italic angle + ticker. The italic pre-scout line under EVERY pending berth specifically threatens the whitespace — three italic compass lines stacked reads closer to a feed than a log. Discipline in implementation (truly subordinate 11px, real line-height, the angle shown for AT MOST the focused/scouting berths rather than all) is what separates this from tipping into the very busyness it claims to avoid.
votes.strongest_element: The gold ligature via framer-motion layoutId="crew-ligature" — a single persona/gold node that physically flies from the focused rail berth's right edge to the body card's left spine (recoloring the real WorkerCard.tsx:273 w-px spine to --gradient-gold). It is the rare case where the literal mechanism (one shared layout element) IS the metaphor (one crew member, one continuous object) IS the craft (one expensive gesture, not ten badges). Graft this even if the concept loses: it solves Q3 more elegantly than any duplicated-highlight or connector-arrow approach, reuses an existing element, and is ~30 lines.
votes.fatal_flaw: The ligature's premium payoff depends entirely on a layoutId measuring correctly across two DISTANT containers — a fixed/sticky-right rail and a separately-scrolling body column. framer-motion shared-layout transitions mis-measure inside transform/overflow/position-context ancestors, and a fixed sidebar + scroll body is exactly that hazard. If it mis-fires, the signature gesture becomes a gold node teleporting to the wrong coordinate or snapping — which reads as BROKEN and cheap, the opposite of the intended effect, and on the one move the whole concept's craft rests on. The concept names this risk and offers a fallback (static gold connector stubs on each side), but the fallback is materially less premium — two stubs pointing at a gap is a diagram, not "one continuous object." So the craft ceiling is real only if the layoutId works in this specific fixed-rail/scroll-body layout; that is an unproven assumption on this exact DOM, not a guaranteed win. Secondary craft erosion: stacking italic --bp-ink-soft pre-scout lines under every pending berth can tip the "calm log" into a busy feed, undercutting the whitespace that makes it feel expensive.

votes.strongest_element: The orthogonal `focusedWorkerId` channel on useAgentAttentionStore wired bidirectionally to reviewCursor (useEffect writes current.id near ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2091; rail click reads + calls setReviewCursor via ordered.findIndex). votes.fatal_flaw: The signature gesture — the framer-motion `layoutId="crew-ligature"` gold node that "physically flies from rail to card" — is the one part that will not work as drawn, and the concept under-rates this as merely risk #1. Verified at page.tsx:111-127: the rail and the body are NOT in a shared layout context — they are separate flex siblings, and the rail lives inside `sticky top-14 ... overflow-y-auto` (page.tsx:120). framer-motion shared-layout animates by measuring bounding boxes and interpolating a transform between two mount points; a `layoutId` element cannot tween across an `overflow-y-auto`/sticky (transformed) clip boundary into an independently-scrolling sibling — it will either clip at the rail's overflow edge, mis-measure under the sticky transform, or simply pop. So the most expensive, identity-defining gesture is precisely the one the real DOM forbids, and the concept's own fallback ("static gold connector stub on each side") quietly abandons the "one continuous object" promise that the whole concept is sold on — leaving two synchronized highlights, which is better than today but is the lesser version. Crucially, this does NOT damage the connectedness verdict: the focus channel + shared promoted-gold persona spine + synchronized dots already make "same crew member" unmistakable without the flying node. Treat the ligature as optional polish, ship the static gold connector + spine + focus channel, and the clarity goal is fully met. concept.name: Command Bridge — 함교 (the lit station rail)
concept.one_line: The sidebar becomes a vertical rail of lit "stations" (one per agent) carrying a real status light + a 4-segment voyage track + a live micro-line; clicking a station docks its full review card in the body with a persistent gold connector tie-line, and selection is two-way synced through one new focusedWorkerId channel on the existing attention store.
concept.big_idea: One organizing idea: every agent is a STATION on a ship's bridge, and the bridge (sidebar) and the captain's table (body review card) are physically wired together. Today the two surfaces already read the same session.workers array (useWorkers, WorkerPanel.tsx:29) but share ZERO focus state — reviewCursor is local to ProgressiveFlow (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:965) and an AgentRow click only toggles its own expandedId (AgentSidebar.tsx:530). The command-bridge makes the wire literal: each station shows the agent's place in the voyage (a 4-segment track: scout → sail → work → reviewed) so "assigned vs actually-working vs awaiting-your-review" is legible at a glance, and the ACTIVE station is visibly tied to the docked card. It feels premium because the whole rail behaves like a single calibrated instrument — slow gold fills, one accent-lit row at a time, a hairline connector that draws itself — rather than a list of chips. It is NOT a generic AI dashboard because nothing blinks gratuitously: motion is reserved for real state changes (a segment filling when status flips, the tie-line drawing on select), using the existing EASE = [0.32,0.72,0,1] and --ease-spring tokens that already define the house's slow, deliberate hand.

concept.connection_mechanic:
A single shared focus channel + a drawn tie-line. Concretely:
1. EXTEND useAgentAttentionStore (useAgentAttentionStore.ts:35) with `focusedWorkerId: string | null` and `setFocusedWorker(id, origin: 'rail'|'body')`. This is the natural home the digest already identified — it is the only cross-surface store, but today it's hover/done-only.
2. In ProgressiveFlow.tsx, make reviewCursor DERIVE from focusedWorkerId instead of being free: when a station is clicked, setFocusedWorker(w.id,'rail'); an effect maps focusedWorkerId → the index in the ordered list and calls setReviewCursor (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2090-2097). Conversely, when the body dots/Prev/Next move the cursor (2111,2143,2149), write focusedWorkerId = ordered[cursor].id with origin 'body'. One source of truth, two writers, no loops (guard on origin).
3. The VISIBLE wire: when a station is focused, (a) the station row gets a left gold spine — a 3px-wide bar on its left edge in --gradient-gold that animates scaleY 0→1; (b) the docked body card grows the SAME gold spine on its left (WorkerReportBlock already has a per-persona color line at WorkerCard.tsx:481 — widen it to 3px and tint --accent when focused); (c) a hairline "tie-line" SVG path draws from the station's right edge toward the body card. Because the rail is a fixed sticky column and the card scrolls, the honest, robust version is a shared gold spine on BOTH ends + a brief AttentionFlash (already imported, AgentSidebar.tsx:14) that pulses station→card on dock, reading as a signal traveling down the wire. Hover mirrors too (cheap, no commit): hovering a station sets a soft ring on the card and vice-versa via the existing isHighlighted path (AgentSidebar.tsx:98-102) extended to honor focusedWorkerId. Result: exactly one accent-lit station, one accent-spined card, unmistakably the same agent.
concept.deploy_ceremony: Keep TeamDeployBanner (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1976-1990) as the gate, but stage it as "the bridge powers up." Pre-deploy, every station light on the rail is a dim navy --bp-ink-soft dot (standby) and each voyage track sits at segment 1 with a faint pre-scout fill. The banner's CTA already exists at TeamDeployBanner.tsx:431-438 (gold gradient). On click → onDeployWorkers (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1259) which already pings 'deploy' (1267). We hook that single ping into a CEREMONY: the rail runs a top-to-bottom ignition sweep — stations light one after another (stagger 0.08s, --ease-spring), each status light going navy→gold→its live color, each voyage track advancing segment 1→2 ("set sail / 출항") with the segment fill animating. A one-line gold rule sweeps down the rail edge (reuse the StageTransitionBanner sweep technique, AgentSidebar.tsx:307-314). The banner itself does a whileTap scale (already 431) then exits upward. So 출항 is not a button press — it's the moment the whole bridge comes alive, row by row, which is the ceremony the owner wanted. Drive it off lastPingSource==='deploy' (already in store, useAgentAttentionStore.ts:56) with a useEffect in AgentSidebar that latches a 1.2s "igniting" flag.
concept.prescout_surfacing: The light pre-scout (Q1) needs a real field: add `pre_scout?: string | null` to WorkerTask (types.ts near ai_preliminary:795) — distinct from ai_preliminary so it never collides with the SELF/human AI reference. During Q&A, right after initWorkers (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1389 / store:872), fire a cheap one-shot per AI worker that returns a single 1-sentence ANGLE (token-frugal — one line, not the task) and store.updateWorker(id,{pre_scout}). In the sidebar, a pre-scouted standby station shows, in its micro-line slot, a quiet compass-prefixed angle: a Compass icon (already used in TeamDeployBanner.tsx:5,156 for assignment_reason — visual rhyme) + the one-line angle in --text-tertiary italic, e.g. "↳ 가격보다 리텐션 곡선부터 보겠습니다." The voyage track's segment 1 fills gold to signal "scout done, ready." Before pre_scout returns, the station shows assignment_reason (already on the worker, init store:926) as the fallback angle so the row is never empty. This means by deploy time every station already shows a direction — the bridge is "warmed up," and the light/cheap nature is the whole point: one sentence, surfaced as a single tertiary line, never the full draft.
concept.status_system:
Per-agent voyage track = 4 segments, each mapped to real WorkerTask.status (types.ts:737) so the visual never lies:
- SEG 1 SCOUT (filled gold when pre_scout present; hollow gold ring while awaiting it): status `pending`/`ai_preparing` pre-deploy. Light = dim navy (--bp-ink-soft) "standby".
- SEG 2 SAIL: set at deploy moment (worker_deploy_phase 'deployed', deployWorkers store:1000). Visual ignition described above.
- SEG 3 WORK (segment pulses/shimmers while filling): status `running`|`sent`|`waiting_response` (the existing isWorkingStatus, AgentSidebar.tsx:27). Light = persona color, AvatarRipple + ShimmerBar (kept, 172,190). `waiting_input` is a SUB-state of seg 3: light → gold pulse + micro-line "입력 필요" (kept badge logic, 48-54) — this is the one state that should also softly pull focus.
- SEG 4 REVIEWED: status `done` fills seg 4 emerald-tinted; then the approved flag refines it — approved===true → seg 4 solid emerald + "반영"; approved===false → seg 4 hollow/struck + "제외" (mirrors WorkerCard.tsx:494-495 and StatusIndicator WorkerPanel.tsx:270-272). `error` → seg 3 turns red with the kept retry affordance (AgentSidebar.tsx:238-247); `validation_failed` → seg 4 amber "확인 필요". A station whose worker is `done && approved==null` (awaiting YOUR review) gets a subtle gold ring + "검토 대기" — these are exactly the remainingToReview set (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2096), so the rail and the "N명 남음" counter agree. The StatusBadge component (AgentSidebar.tsx:31) is reused as the light+label engine; the 4-segment track is the only net-new visual.

votes.verdict: Verified against source: every citation holds. The attention store genuinely has no focus channel (useAgentAttentionStore.ts:35-51 is hover+ping only), reviewCursor is a free local useState (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:965), the WorkerCard color line is a w-px hairline (WorkerCard.tsx:481), deploy pings 'deploy' (1267), and the rail is w-72 xl:w-80 sticky (page.tsx:120). The structural diagnosis is correct and the focusedWorkerId-with-origin-guard is the right, minimal mechanic. On CONNECTEDNESS the concept is strong: one shared channel, two-way, origin-guarded against loops, with a committed shared-gold-spine fallback when the SVG tie-line geometry breaks — that honesty is mature. On DNA it stays on-brand (navy --bp-ink-soft for standby instead of gray, gold gradient fills, reuses EASE/--ease-spring, motion-only-on-real-transitions). But on CRAFT-PREMIUM — the lens I must judge — this concept is the BUSIEST of the family and that is a real liability. Per station row it stacks FIVE simultaneous signals: a 7px status light, the avatar (with ripple), name+Lv pill, a swapping micro-line, AND a 4-segment voyage track + chevron — inside a 256-288px content width (w-72 minus p-4). The mockup itself betrays the density: '●─●─◍─○', '◌gold', '검토 대기', '반영 ✓' all competing in one 2-line row. That is closer to a flight-instrument cluster than the generous-whitespace, editorial dawn-harbor DNA. The 4-segment track is the single net-new element and it is the one that risks reading as a 'progress widget' — a generic-dashboard tell — rather than something expensive and quiet. A premium rail would express scout→sail→work→reviewed with ONE calibrated cue (the status light's color + a single fill), not a four-dot ASCII track that the eye has to parse. concept.name: 해도 크루 (Crew Chart) — the rail becomes a navigator's star-chart; the lit leg is the link
concept.one_line: The right rail stops being a list of cards and becomes a vertical star-chart: each agent is a charted waypoint on the voyage line, the pre-scout shows as a faint pencilled bearing under each star, "set sail" lights the whole route at once, and clicking any star draws a single lit gold leg straight to the focused review card in the body — sidebar and body are now visibly one constellation.
concept.big_idea: Argus already owns a nautical chart language (VoyageChart.tsx:48 — the 해도, with logged points as filled gold dots, checkpoints as hollow rings, the "current" node ringed, anchored legs flagged). The worker rail today throws that away and reverts to a generic stack of bordered cards (AgentSidebar AgentRow, 138-249) — exactly the "generic AI dashboard" we're told NOT to be. The big idea: re-skin the rail as a STAR-CHART of the crew. The voyage line runs top-to-bottom; each agent is a star/waypoint pinned on it in step_index order; the line between stars IS the progress bar (it currently floats disconnected at 474). The chart is the navigator — it carries rich per-agent status as the star's own state (unlit→pencilled→lit→flagged), and it IS the thing that connects to the body: selecting a star runs a lit gold leg out of the rail toward the focused review card. It feels premium because nothing is a "widget" — it's one continuous drawn route on aged-chart vellum, ink + gold, that earns the voyage DNA instead of decorating around it. Reuse, not reinvention: same dot/ring/flag vocabulary, same --accent gold, same EASE.
concept.sidebar_design: The rail (workspace/page.tsx:120, w-72/xl:w-80, under Logbook) becomes a single vertical chart column, not a list of separate cards. STRUCTURE, top→bottom: (1) Header eyebrow "해도 · 크루 / Crew Chart" with the live count chip kept from AgentSidebar:449-471. (2) A single drawn VOYAGE SPINE — a 2px vertical line down the left third (x≈22px), rendered as the existing --gradient-gold but masked so only the traversed portion (origin→last done star) is gold and the rest is --border-subtle ink. This spine REPLACES the floating progress bar at 474-482 — progress is now literally how far the gold has climbed the route. (3) Each agent is a STAR-ROW pinned on the spine: a node glyph sitting ON the spine at left, then a flush content block to its right. The content block per row is two-tier and richer than today: line 1 = persona name + Lv badge (reuse agent-lv class, AgentSidebar:198-202) + a right-aligned StarStatus glyph (see status_system); line 2 = the live line — pre-scout bearing when pencilled, the genuine stream tail when working (reuse tailSnippet + tickersFor, AgentSidebar:65/109), the key finding when done (reuse extractKeyFinding). (4) NO more filtering pending workers out (kill visibleWorkers at 433) — the whole point of a chart is you see the full planned route from the start, faint stars and all. (5) Multi-stage grouping stays but renders as labelled SEGMENTS of the same spine (reuse StageDivider, 343, as a "Stage Ⅱ" tick on the line rather than a free-floating divider). The row is no longer a bordered card with its own shadow; selected state is carried by the LEG, not a box — so the rail reads as one object.
concept.connection_mechanic: A real shared focus channel plus a drawn gold leg. MECHANIC: extend useAgentAttentionStore (useAgentAttentionStore.ts:35) with one field — `focusedWorkerId: string | null` + `setFocusedWorker(id)`. This is the natural home the digest already flagged. WIRING: (a) the body stepper's reviewCursor (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2090) becomes derived/synced — on cursor change it calls setFocusedWorker(current.id); conversely clicking a star calls setFocusedWorker(w.id) AND the stepper reads focusedWorkerId to set its cursor (find the ordered index, setReviewCursor). One source of truth, bidirectional. (b) THE VISIBLE LINK — the focused star is the only lit-bright node; from it, a single gold leg animates: a thin horizontal --gradient-gold line draws from the star's node OUT to the right edge of the rail (the rail's left border, page.tsx:120, becomes the "shore"), and the focused WorkerReportBlock in the body grows a matching 2px gold left-edge rail (replace its neutral persona color-line at WorkerCard.tsx:462 with --gradient-gold WHEN focused) plus a small gold node dot at its top-left that visually "receives" the leg. Same gold, same y-rhythm: the eye reads star→leg→card as one stroke. (c) The non-focused stars dim to 0.5 (reuse the existing isDimmed pattern, AgentSidebar:102/144) so the lit path is unmistakable. (d) Hover (not click) does a lighter version: a 1px dashed bearing-line ghosts toward the body and the matching card gets a faint ring — reusing the bi-directional hover the store already does for attribution (AgentSidebar:98-101). Click = lock (lit solid leg, the sticky mechanic already exists at setHovered(…, true)/clearHovered, store:60-69). This is professional because it's ONE accent, ONE line weight, deterministic geometry — not glow soup.
concept.deploy_ceremony: Keep the gate (TeamDeployBanner, ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1976-1989, deployPhase 'ready'→'deployed') but make the moment a CHART event, not just a button. The TeamDeployBanner stays as the editable crew manifest pre-deploy (its group/track/swap logic at 252-401 is load-bearing — untouched). The CEREMONY is what the rail does on deploy: at deployPhase 'ready' the spine is drawn but UNLIT (pencil-grey), every star pencilled/hollow. When the user clicks "팀 투입 / Set sail" (relabel CTA at 437 to L('출항','Set sail') — the owner wants the 출항 word), fire one sequenced animation, gated behind a 700ms ceremony before runAllAIWorkers actually streams: (1) a single light sweeps DOWN the whole spine origin→destination (reuse the StageTransitionBanner sweep, AgentSidebar:308-314, rotated vertical) turning the route from pencil to gold leg-by-leg with stagger delay i*0.12 on EASE; (2) each star "lights" as the sweep passes it — scale 0.9→1, hollow→filled, with the AvatarRipple (AgentVisuals) firing once per star in persona color; (3) a one-time caption crossfades in the rail header: "항로 확정 · 출항 / Course set · underway", auto-hiding after 2.5s (reuse the 4s banner pattern, AgentSidebar:415-417). Also fire useAgentAttentionStore.ping('deploy') (already a PingSource, store:22) so every star flashes gold once in unison — the crew acknowledging the captain. It's a real scene: the map goes from a drafted plan to a lit, sailing route in one breath. Cheap to build (all reused primitives), expensive to feel.
concept.prescout_surfacing: The light pre-scout writes to the existing `ai_preliminary` field (types.ts:795 — already there, no new type/migration needed) during Q&A after initWorkers, with a tiny status flag `ai_preliminary_status?: 'scouting'|'ready'` (one net-new optional field, CLAUDE.md checklist: types + createWorker default + the prescout call site). SURFACING in the rail: while a pre-scout runs, the agent's star is HOLLOW with a slow pencil-stroke shimmer around its ring (reuse ShimmerBar, AgentVisuals, drawn as a ring instead of a bar) and line 2 reads a quiet ticker "방향 잡는 중 / sketching an angle" (reuse tickersFor). When ai_preliminary lands, the star stays hollow but gains a faint gold pencil tick mark beside it (a half-filled node — half ink, half gold, distinct from the solid "done" star) and line 2 shows the bearing: the pre-scout one-liner italic, prefixed with a tiny Compass (lucide, already imported in TeamDeployBanner:5) — e.g. "↳ 경쟁사 가격 구조부터 본다 / start from competitor pricing". So by deploy time every star already shows a DIRECTION (a pencilled bearing on the chart), making "this crew has already oriented itself" legible — and the contrast pencil→lit at set-sail is what sells the ceremony. "Light" stays light: it's one short line per agent, no full task, frugal.
concept.status_system: One node-glyph vocabulary mapped 1:1 to real WorkerStatus (types.ts:737), borrowing VoyageChart's dot/ring/flag legend (VoyageChart.tsx:136-158) so it's already a learned language: • pending (assigned, no scout yet) → small HOLLOW grey ring, dim 0.55, line2 = assigned task. • ai_preliminary_status 'scouting' (pre-scout running) → hollow ring + slow pencil shimmer, line2 = "sketching an angle". • pre-scout ready (still pending) → HALF node (ink+gold pencil tick) + italic bearing line. • ai_preparing → same half/scouting treatment (AI aux pre-pass, store:1010) — honest, it IS preparing. • running / sent / waiting_response → LIT node pulsing in persona color + AvatarRipple + live stream tail (reuse isWorkingStatus, AgentSidebar:27; the gold spine has climbed to this star). • waiting_input → lit node with a gold pulsing dot + "입력 필요 / Input" pill (keep StatusBadge logic, AgentSidebar:48-54) — the one star that asks the captain for a heading. • done → SOLID GOLD FILLED star (the VoyageChart "logged point", 138) + completion_note italic; if awaiting review (approved==null) a faint gold ring orbits it = "logged, not yet confirmed". • approved===true → solid star with a small Flag/anchor (reuse Flag, VoyageChart:116) = "course reflected in the draft". • approved===false → hollow dimmed node, struck (the "abandoned course" treatment, VoyageChart:153) = excluded. • error / validation_failed → node ringed red + inline Retry (keep AgentSidebar:238-247). The captain reads the whole journey assigned→scouting→ready→[set sail]→working→done→awaiting-review→reviewed as the star's own life on the line — no separate legend needed because it mirrors the chart they already know.

votes.verdict: This is the most craft-premium concept on the table, and it earns the score by ELIMINATING widgets rather than decorating them. The single load-bearing insight — "nothing is a card; it's one continuous drawn route on aged-chart vellum" — is exactly the move that separates expensive from generic-dashboard. It kills the three things that currently make the rail read cheap: (a) the floating disconnected progress bar at AgentSidebar:474-482, replaced by progress-as-traversed-spine (literal, not metaphorical — the gold IS the bar); (b) the stack of individually-bordered, individually-shadowed cards at AgentRow:163-169 (every row a competing box with its own ring + shadow-[0_0_22px] glow — that 22px glow soup is precisely the busy/cheap tell), replaced by ONE object whose only selected-state signal is the leg, not a box; (c) the emerald/green completion language (AgentRow:165, StatusBadge:42-46) which is OFF-DNA — green checkmarks are the generic-AI-dashboard vocabulary, and this concept correctly retires them for the chart's own gold-fill/hollow-ring/flag legend (VoyageChart:136-158), a vocabulary the product ALREADY teaches elsewhere so it costs zero learning. Hierarchy is disciplined: ONE accent (--accent #96782e / --gradient-gold), ONE line weight (2px spine, 2px leg, 2px card rail — same stroke read top to bottom), deterministic geometry instead of glow. That is the definition of restrained. Whitespace improves because rows lose their bordered chrome and breathe on the spine. The motion spec is genuinely elegant: the set-sail sweep (rotated StageTransitionBanner sweep, AgentSidebar:308-314) turning pencil→gold leg-by-leg at stagger i*0.12 on EASE [0.32,0.72,0,1] is slow, drawn, single-accent — the "drafted plan → lit sailing route in one breath" is a real scene, not a button flash, and it makes the deploy gate a ceremony as the owner asked. The pencil→lit contrast is the smartest craft decision: it gives the pre-scout a VISUAL PAYOFF at set-sail, so the frugal light pass isn't just a token-saver, it's the thing that makes the ceremony land. DNA fidelity is total: this is the only concept that stops decorating AROUND the voyage metaphor and makes the rail BE the 해도. On craft alone, restrained, intentional, expensive — yes.
votes.strongest_element: The progress-bar-becomes-spine substitution: deleting the floating bar at AgentSidebar:474-482 and making "how far the gold has climbed the route" the literal progress indicator. This is craft of the highest order — one element doing two jobs with zero added chrome — and it is graftable into ANY competing concept independently of the star-chart skin. It single-handedly removes the most generic-dashboard element in the current rail.
votes.fatal_flaw: Not fatal but the one genuine craft risk: un-filtering pending workers (deleting visibleWorkers at AgentSidebar:433) so the FULL route shows from the start. On a 5–6 agent crew with multi-stage grouping, a vertical column of hollow stars + pencilled italic bearing lines + StarStatus glyphs + Lv badges is a LOT of faint marks competing before anything is lit — the exact busy-ness the lens punishes. The proposed mitigation (dim hollow stars to 0.5–0.55) is necessary but may not be sufficient: dimmed-but-present text still reads as visual noise on a cream/ivory bg where low-contrast grey ink doesn't recede as cleanly as it would on dark. The premium version needs the unlit pre-deploy state to be genuinely SPARSE — bearings possibly collapsed to a single glyph until hover/focus, names tracked tighter, the spine doing most of the talking — or the "full planned route" virtue tips into a cluttered chart that undercuts the whole expensive-restraint thesis. Tune the unlit density hard or this concept's signature move (show the whole route) becomes its own craft liability.

votes.verdict: On the connectedness-clarity lens this is the strongest entry I can imagine for the "one team, status↔action" mandate, but it is not flawless. What it nails: the per-agent journey (assigned→scouting→ready→working→done→awaiting-review→reviewed) is mapped 1:1 onto a SINGLE node vocabulary that Argus users ALREADY know — VoyageChart's filled-dot/hollow-ring/ringed-current/flag/abandoned legend (verified VoyageChart.tsx:136-158). That is the cleverest move in the whole field: status legibility comes for free because it reuses a learned language, so a first-timer who has seen the 해도 reads the crew's state without a key. The spine-as-progress is a genuine improvement over today's disconnected floating bar (verified AgentSidebar.tsx:474-482) — "how far the gold has climbed" is more legible than a percentage. The connection mechanic is real, not decorative: extending useAgentAttentionStore with focusedWorkerId + bidirectional sync to reviewCursor (verified the store has the sticky-hover plumbing at :60-69 and the stepper has setReviewCursor + clickable dots at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2090-2143) is one source of truth done correctly. The gold-leg + matching card left-rail (swapping the existing persona color-line, verified WorkerCard.tsx:480-482) makes the sidebar↔body link visible with ONE accent and deterministic geometry — exactly "not glow soup." Where it loses a point on THIS lens: (1) the link is associative, not continuous — by the concept's own (correct, verified) risk mitigation, the gold leg stops at the rail's "shore" and the card answers with a matching rail; the eye must complete the constellation. That is robust engineering but it IS a weaker form of "unmistakable" than a literal drawn line, and for a true first-timer the same-gold-same-y-rhythm cue may not fully land on first contact. (2) The mechanic is desktop-only: the rail is hidden lg:block (verified page.tsx:120), and on tablet/mobile a WorkerDrawer takes over (page.tsx:133) — the concept never addresses how "one team, status↔action" survives there, so a chunk of users get NONE of the connection. Net: it makes status MORE legible than any rival and the deploy moment genuinely legible (pencil→lit sweep with an 출항 caption is unambiguous), but the body↔rail link is "strongly implied," not literally traced.

votes.verdict: Strongest concept I've judged against this lens: it earns the voyage DNA instead of decorating around it. The core insight is verified and correct — Argus already owns a complete nautical-node vocabulary (VoyageChart/BranchMap.tsx:93-124: filled=logged point, hollow=surface, ring=active checkpoint, Flag=anchored, opacity-dim=abandoned), and the worker rail today throws it away for generic bordered cards (AgentSidebar AgentRow:138-249, rounded-xl border + shadow per row — exactly the "generic AI dashboard" we're told not to be). Reskinning the rail's row-stack into one drawn spine with that SAME glyph set is the rare proposal that is both more premium AND more on-brand AND reuse-heavy. DNA fidelity is a clean 5: single accent (--accent #96782e + --gradient-gold), one line weight, the spine literally REPLACING the floating progress bar at AgentSidebar:474-482 so progress becomes "how far the gold has climbed" — that is genuinely intentional, not widget soup. CONNECTION is the strongest part and it is real, not hand-waved: I verified reviewCursor/setReviewCursor exist (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:965, 989, 2090-2097), the stepper dots ALREADY call setReviewCursor(i) at 2111, and WorkerReportBlock renders at 2128 — so the bidirectional focus sync (add focusedWorkerId to useAgentAttentionStore:35, stepper writes on cursor change + reads to drive setReviewCursor) really is ~15 lines, and the sticky-lock / clear-on-click-outside plumbing already exists (store:60-69, 80-95). ping('deploy') is already a declared PingSource (store:18-27), so the unison deploy flash is free. BUILDABILITY is a 4 not 5 for three honest reasons. (1) Citation drift: the proposal repeatedly cites "WorkerCard.tsx:462 neutral persona color-line" — the actual color line is at 480-482 and is NOT neutral, it already uses persona?.color; the swap-to-gold-when-focused is still trivial (conditional style) but the author clearly eyeballed line numbers rather than re-reading, which lowers my confidence that other cited line ranges (AgentSidebar:308-314 sweep, 175-182 completion bar) were all freshly verified. (2) The biggest real risk — a continuous gold line spanning two independent scroll containers (rail is sticky overflow-y-auto at page.tsx:120; body is a separate overflow-y-auto at 877) — IS correctly identified and correctly mitigated in the concept's own risk section: don't span containers, draw a gold stub to the rail's shore-edge and have the card answer with a matching --gradient-gold left-rail + receiving node. That mitigation matches the actual DOM I verified and is robust. Good. (3) The spine-as-SVG-or-border layout rewrite of a grouped, stage-segmented, AnimatePresence-driven row stack (AgentSidebar:505-551) is more than a reskin — pinning nodes ON a continuous spine at correct y-offsets while keeping StageDivider as inline "Stage Ⅱ" ticks, multi-stage grouping, and per-row enter stagger is fiddly geometry. Buildable in the claimed ~1 day, but the estimate is optimistic if stage grouping and the leg's absolute y-anchoring to a scrolling star both have to be pixel-correct. Net: faithful, mostly reuse, one genuine layout rewrite, no new deps, no migration. A clear build-it.
votes.strongest_element: The spine-replaces-progress-bar move plus the shared-focus channel. Even if the full star-chart reskin is descoped, two grafts stand alone and are nearly free: (a) kill the floating progress bar at AgentSidebar:474-482 and render progress as a single vertical gold spine the rows pin to — instantly makes the rail read as ONE object instead of a card stack; (b) add focusedWorkerId + setFocusedWorker to useAgentAttentionStore and bidirectionally sync it with the stepper's existing reviewCursor (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2090-2111) — this delivers the core "status↔action, one team" ask with ~15 lines and zero new infrastructure, independent of any chart aesthetic. Graft these even if the concept loses.
votes.fatal_flaw: Not fatal, but the load-bearing weakness is the pre-scout's honesty-vs-frugality bind, and it routes through a field collision. The concept reuses the EXISTING ai_preliminary field (types.ts:795) for a NEW meaning. But ai_preliminary is already semantically owned: it holds the AI-assisted preliminary for HUMAN/self tasks and is consumed as such in live code (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1219/1280/1283, WorkerCard.tsx:301/368/454/648, store:1732 buildContext tags it type:'preliminary'). Writing an all-agents Q&A "bearing" into the same field risks the human-task surfaces (the waiting_input card content at WorkerCard:454, and the buildContext at store:1732) mistaking a cheap scout-sketch for a real preliminary analysis — that is precisely the "theater that misleads" the codebase explicitly guards against (AgentSidebar:104-108 honesty note). The proposed ai_preliminary_status flag helps gate the UI but does NOT disambiguate the field's MEANING for the existing consumers. The concept also leans on the pre-scout being "genuinely LIGHT/token-frugal," but the surfacing is the only thing it actually designs — the LLM call itself is hand-waved as "product work." A per-agent extra LLM pass during Q&A (when the user is also driving runInitialAnalysis + Q&A turns) is N more calls before any deploy value is committed; "one short line per agent" keeps OUTPUT tokens low but says nothing about INPUT context cost (each scout still needs the framing + that agent's task injected), so "frugal" is asserted, not demonstrated. Fix is cheap and keeps the whole design: give the pre-scout its OWN optional field (e.g. ai_scout_bearing) per the CLAUDE.md add-a-field checklist rather than overloading ai_preliminary, and spec the scout as a SINGLE batched call returning one bearing per agent (one prompt, N short lines out) rather than N calls — that makes "light" real and removes the collision. With that, the concept has no fatal flaw.

concept.name: 단일 항로 (THE SINGLE SPINE / "항로")
concept.one_line: The sidebar becomes a literal vertical voyage-route — each agent is a station on one gold spine; pre-scout glows faintly under its node, "출항" lights the whole route, work flows down it, and clicking any station docks its review card to that exact node in the body so the rail and the card are one continuous line.
concept.big_idea: Stop treating the rail and the review stepper as two surfaces to "connect" — make them two ends of ONE drawn line. The right rail (workspace/page.tsx:120 `w-72 xl:w-80` sticky rail) becomes a vertical "항로" (route): a single 2px spine in `--gradient-gold` runs top-to-bottom with a node per agent (one node = one WorkerTask, ordered by `step_index`). The body review stepper is not a separate widget — it is the *currently-docked station* of that same route, rendered inline in the column but visually tethered to its rail node by a shared gold thread + a synced `focusedWorkerId`. Premium because: (1) it is a single editorial object, not a dashboard of cards — serif station labels, generous vertical rhythm, one continuous gold line that literally draws itself as the voyage progresses (reusing the existing `draw-line`/`bar-grow` motion language at globals.css:351/410); (2) the connection is *structural*, not a highlight bolted on — you are always looking at one route, and "which station am I at" is answered by where the line is lit, not by two independent glows; (3) it turns the agreed metaphor (reframe→...→이타카) into the actual geometry of the screen. It feels expensive because nothing is crude or duplicated: status, pre-scout, deploy ceremony, and review all live on ONE drawn spine.
concept.sidebar_design: AgentSidebar.tsx is reworked from a list of bordered cards into a vertical route. Structure: a left gutter (16px) holds the continuous spine — a 2px line `bg-[var(--border-subtle)]` with a gold "filled" overlay (`--gradient-gold`) whose height = (lit progress) animated like the existing progress bar (474-482) but rotated vertical. Each agent is a **station node** sitting on the spine: an 18px node ring (the existing WorkerAvatar size="sm" centered in a ring whose color = `worker.persona.color` or `--accent`). To the right of each node: station label block — serif `--font-display` agent name at 13px, role/Lv as a quiet sub-line (reuse `agent-lv` class + `localizePersona`). Below the label, a single status line (the rich status, see status_system) and, when working, the existing live ticker (`tickersFor`/`stream_text` tail, reuse 109-121 verbatim) and `ShimmerBar`. CRITICAL CHANGE: remove the `visibleWorkers` filter at AgentSidebar.tsx:433 — pending/pre-scout agents are NO LONGER hidden. The whole point of a route is you see all stations from the start as faint, unlit nodes; they brighten as the voyage reaches them. Header keeps "분석 팀 / Analysis Team" eyebrow but the 2px horizontal progress bar (474-482) is removed (the spine IS the progress now). Stage grouping (`groupedByStage`, 437) survives as labeled spine *segments* — the StageDivider (343) becomes a station marker on the spine ("Stage Ⅱ — 검증") with the gold line passing through it.
concept.connection_mechanic: Extend `useAgentAttentionStore` (useAgentAttentionStore.ts:53) with ONE new channel — `focusedWorkerId: string | null` + `setFocusedWorker(id)` — the natural shared-focus home the digest already identified. This is the spine's "current station." Wiring: (1) Body stepper (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2086) stops owning focus locally — `reviewCursor` (965) is DERIVED from `focusedWorkerId` (find its index in the ordered list) and the dots/Prev/Later call `setFocusedWorker(orderedId)` instead of `setReviewCursor`. (2) Clicking any rail station node calls `setFocusedWorker(w.id)` — this is the new behavior replacing the row's local `expandedId` toggle (529-530). (3) The focused station and its docked body card share a literal **gold tether**: the focused node grows a `--gradient-gold` connector that runs from the rail node horizontally to the body card's left color-line (WorkerCard.tsx:481 already renders a `w-px self-stretch` persona-color line — we light it gold when `worker.id === focusedWorkerId`). On desktop the rail is `sticky top-14` (page.tsx:120) so the node stays pinned beside its card; we draw the connector with a single `motion.div` (a 1px gold horizontal rule + a soft `--shadow-md` glow) that animates `scaleX` 0→1 with `EASE` when focus lands. (4) Bi-directional highlight: focused node gets `ring-2 ring-[var(--accent)]/60` + the same `shadow-[0_0_22px_-4px_rgba(180,160,100,0.35)]` already used for `isHighlighted` (AgentSidebar.tsx:164) so it matches existing polish; the docked card gets a matching gold left-line + a faint `--gradient-gold-subtle` wash. Result: there is never ambiguity — the lit node, the tether, and the open card are one unbroken gold path. Hover-attribution (`hovered`) stays untouched for draft↔agent attribution; focus is a separate, persistent channel so the two never fight.
concept.deploy_ceremony: Kept as a hard gate, designed as a real scene — "출항" (set sail). Pre-deploy (`deployPhase==='ready'`) the spine exists but is UNLIT: nodes are present but desaturated (persona color at 35% via `opacity`), the spine line is `--border-subtle` only, and a docked "harbor" card at the bottom of the route is the TeamDeployBanner (already rendered at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1976) — restyled so its primary CTA reads **출항** again (revert TeamDeployBanner.tsx:437 label to `L('출항', 'Set sail')` with the existing `Compass` icon instead of `ChevronRight`). The ceremony: on click `onDeploy`, before `store.deployWorkers()` fires, play a 1.1s "cast off" sequence — the gold spine *draws itself top-to-bottom* (a `motion.div` masking the gold overlay, `scaleY` 0→1 from origin-top, `--ease-wave`, ~0.9s, reusing the `draw-line` keyframe feel at globals.css:351), each station node "lighting" in sequence as the line reaches it (staggered `boxShadow` pop + persona-color saturating 35%→100%, stagger 0.08s by `step_index`), and a single soft gold sweep travels down the spine (the same sweep technique as StageTransitionBanner.tsx:308-314, rotated vertical). Fire `useAgentAttentionStore.ping('deploy')` (already a valid PingSource, line 22) at sequence start so every node flashes via the existing `AttentionFlash`/`useAttentionPulse`. The banner does a `whileTap scale:0.98` (already there) then collapses upward into the now-lit route. It is a genuine moment — the voyage line comes alive — not a spinner. After the sequence, `deployWorkers()` flips statuses and the first running node begins streaming.
concept.prescout_surfacing: Light pre-scout surfaces as a faint "sketch" tucked UNDER each station node before deploy. Data: reuse the existing `ai_preliminary?: string | null` field (types.ts:795 — the digest confirms it exists and is unused at deploy time) — the Q1 light pass writes a 1-line angle per agent into `worker.ai_preliminary`. In the rail, when `deployPhase==='ready'` and `worker.ai_preliminary` is set, render it directly under the station label as a single dim line: 11px, `text-[var(--text-tertiary)]`, italic, prefixed by a tiny `Compass` glyph (matching the existing assignment_reason treatment at TeamDeployBanner.tsx:156) — e.g. "예상 각도: 가격보다 전환 마찰을 먼저 본다". It is intentionally faint (opacity ~0.7) and short — "light is the whole point." Visual state: a pre-scouted node shows a **hollow gold ring with a single dotted arc** (CSS `border-dashed`) — signaling "has a direction, not yet sailed." While the pre-scout is still computing, the node shows a quiet `TypingDots` under the label and status `ai_preparing`-style. This means by 출항 time every station already reads as "knows its heading," and deploy visibly converts the dashed pre-scout ring into a solid lit node — the dashed→solid transition is the visual promise being kept.
concept.status_system: Per-station visual language mapped to real WorkerStatus (types.ts:737) + `approved`, expressed as node-ring state + one status line. (1) pending (assigned, pre-deploy): hollow desaturated ring, persona color @35%, label dim; status line = task name (reuse 233-235). (2) pre-scout present (pending + `ai_preliminary` set): hollow **dashed gold** ring; sub-line shows the angle (see prescout). (3) ai_preparing: ring pulses, `TypingDots`, line "AI 참고자료 준비 중" (reuse WorkerCard.tsx:211 wording). (4) running / sent / waiting_response (`isWorkingStatus`, 27-29): **lit node** — solid persona-color ring with `AvatarRipple` + `ShimmerBar` on the spine segment below it, live ticker line, and the spine gold-fill animates DOWN to this node (the "work flowing down the route"); badge = the existing spinning `live` pill (35-39). (5) waiting_input: gold pulsing dot + "입력 필요" (reuse 48-54) — node ring turns solid gold (`--accent`), and because it needs the captain, it auto-becomes the focused station. (6) done (un-reviewed): emerald check node (reuse 41-46), spine segment above it now solid gold; sub-line = `completion_note` (222-226); a faint "검토 대기 / awaiting review" tag. (7) reviewed-approved (`approved===true`): node fills solid gold with a small "반영" tag (mirror WorkerCard.tsx:494); spine segment locks gold. (8) reviewed-excluded (`approved===false`): node dims to `--border-subtle`, label `line-through`-soft, "제외" tag (mirror 495) — the station is visibly skipped on the route. (9) error: red ring + inline Retry (reuse 238-247) — a "rough water" station. (10) validation_failed: amber ring, "품질 확인 필요" (reuse WorkerCard.tsx:193). The reviewed states are the new richness the rail was missing — the route now shows the full journey assigned→scouting→ready→sailing→done→reviewed at a glance.

Whitespace and hierarchy are respected because the status-rail (2px persona-color margin bar encoding lifecycle by opacity) carries state WITHOUT adding visual noise — it doubles as the thread's docking point, which is elegant economy. That is "status↔action, one team" made literally true in data AND mirrored in a single ring (the exact :164 hover ring) plus one disciplined gold thread. A first-timer would unmistakably read the sidebar and body as the same crew. The single highest-leverage move is also correctly identified: deleting the `visibleWorkers = workers.filter(w => !isPending(w))` cut at AgentSidebar.tsx:433 — that one line is most of the "assigned vs working" illegibility, and the status-rail fill + StatusBadge extension (verified the else-branch is already "대기/standby" at :59) cleanly maps the journey assigned→working→done→reviewed, with done+approved/rejected mirrored back from the body (closing the loop). The rail becomes one editorial gold spine where each agent is a station with a calm voyage-status node (progress = how far the gold has climbed, replacing the floating bar). CONNECTION MECHANIC (3 lines):
- One new orthogonal `focusedWorkerId` channel on useAgentAttentionStore; the body stepper's reviewCursor becomes its projection (body writes current.id; rail click writes reviewCursor via ordered.findIndex) — bidirectional, no loop, hover untouched.

- One assertive gesture: a one-shot SVG thread (1.5px gold, pathLength 0→1 over 0.5s EASE, hold 700ms, fade) drawn station→card on focus-change, never tracked — degrades to the dual spine when it can't measure.

2. Delete the pending filter at AgentSidebar.tsx:433 and render the full crew with a quiet standby treatment (fixes most "assigned vs working" illegibility, safe alone).
3. Wire bidirectional focus sync: useEffect in the stepper (~ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2091) pushes current.id → setFocusedWorker; rail row onClick sets focus + setReviewCursor(ordered.findIndex). With the pending filter deleted (§2/Step 2), a long crew at varying opacities risks reading busy unless the "quiet standby" treatment (opacity 0.55-0.7, no ticker, compact) is genuinely restrained. FocusThread depends on an SVG gradient def that is named but not specified.
